A1.justification: The PDFs describe the same group-operation interpretability study despite the changed title and organization. Both provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices sufficient for reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original training and verification results for 100 S5 networks (Section 6.2, Figure 3), plus causal-intervention results aggregated over 128 Z/53Z runs (Table 1).

after.justification: v3 reports original S5 results, additional S4 and A5 verification experiments, parameter-replacement analyses, and loss-bound experiments, alongside the retained causal-intervention results.

M1.justification: The network architecture, ρ-set and sign circuits, and accuracy-verification procedure are retained. Appendix J adds limited adaptations that produce cross-entropy upper bounds from margins or from idealized-model loss combined with logit-distance bounds.

E1.justification: v1 quantitatively evaluates compact proofs on S5 and separately studies causal interventions on Z/53Z. v3 adds compact-proof evaluations on S4 and the alternating group A5 (Appendix K.1, Figures 10–11), substantially broadening verification coverage beyond the original symmetric-group case. The preliminary complex/quaternionic observations are retained.

E2.justification: The principal Vbrute and Vcoset comparators and the comparison with Stander et al. in Table 1 remain. The new bi-equivariance experiment adds randomly initialized networks as an evaluated reference alongside original and idealized networks (Figure 6).

E3.justification: The stated S5 training setup is unchanged. New experiments introduce parameter- and irrep-specific replacement protocols, a bi-equivariance metric, and loss-bound evaluation. Appendix I specifies distinct added settings: S4 uses width 64 and an 80% training fraction; A5 uses width 256, weight decay 10^-6, and no unembedding bias.

E4.justification: New Appendix C tests parameter agreement with idealized circuits, measures bi-equivariance, and examines loss after replacing selected parameter types or irrep-specific neurons (Figures 5–8). Appendix J additionally tests whether accuracy-proof techniques yield useful loss bounds. The earlier projection-vector analysis and causal-intervention study are retained.

E5.justification: Figures 5–6 newly provide box-and-whisker summaries of between-model variability in parameter mismatch and bi-equivariance. The 100-run S5 and 128-run intervention counts were already reported in v1; v3 introduces no confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figure 3 changes the all-model mean accuracy bound from 51.0% to 50.4%, and mean Vbrute/Virrep runtimes from 2.01/0.61 to 2.20/0.75 seconds. The explained-only mean changes from 82.3% to 91.7%, but its retained population changes from 62% to 55%, preventing a same-population improvement claim. v3 also adds mechanism-diagnostic results, S4/A5 verification results, and unsuccessful cross-entropy bounds.

T1.justification: v3 adds auxiliary proofs of cross-entropy Lipschitzness and smoothness (Lemmas G.3–G.4), loss-bound derivations, and a formal bi-equivariance diagnostic. Observation B.2 adds approximately equal embedding-coefficient norms and revises the associated scaling expression. The main group-theoretic results and accuracy-verifier proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The main claims about ρ-set circuits, approximate bi-equivariance, and compact verification remain. v3 modestly qualifies the abstract and contribution list from unifying previous explanations to a step toward unification, and explicitly restricts the headline numerical guarantee to S5.

C2.justification: Appendix K.1 adds an explanation linking larger relative ρ-set sizes to missing-pair failures. Appendix J explains the poor loss bounds and emphasizes choosing a task-relevant property to verify. Section 7 additionally distinguishes proof compression from causal-intervention faithfulness; the earlier limitations and failure explanations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B.4 expands v1's terse reconstruction description into a detailed walkthrough using regression, singular-value decomposition, clustering, and structural checks. Appendix I newly documents clustering fragility, repeated reconstruction attempts with selection by the highest verified bound, and S4/A5 hyperparameters. These disclosures substantially improve reproducibility without establishing that the underlying reconstruction procedure changed.

R1.justification: v3 adds Beck (2017) and Boyd and Vandenberghe (2004) for the loss proofs, and replaces Geiger et al. (2024) with Chan et al. (2022) as the causal-scrubbing reference. Its central positioning relative to Chughtai et al. and Stander et al. remains substantially the same.

P1.justification: v3 retitles the paper, expands the introduction's explanation of compact proofs, and presents its circuit and verification before revisiting previous explanations. The former relationship discussion moves into Section 6.3, and Appendix B gains a substantially expanded, subdivided discovery narrative. This is significant reorganization beyond renumbering.

P2.justification: Figure 1 replaces the conceptual S3 algorithm diagram with extracted S4/A5 ρ-set visualizations. Seven additional figures display parameter agreement, equivariance, replacement analyses, loss bounds, and additional-group results. The three existing tables remain, while the expanded figure set substantially changes the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens evidence and reproducibility beyond v1's predominantly S5 verification study. Appendix C directly tests the proposed mechanism, B.4 and I make its reconstruction much more reproducible, and S4/A5 experiments test applicability beyond the main case. Reporting unsuccessful loss bounds and group-dependent failures also clarifies the explanation's limits. These gains support a substantial quality improvement despite the retained core method and mixed numerical updates.
